snippet.title: Harpooning for Survival | Lamalera: Indonesia's Last Whaling Culture | Free Documentary
snippet.description:
Harpooning for Survival | Lamalera: Indonesia's Last Whaling Culture | Free Documentary

Bhutan - Life Between the Middle Ages and the Modern World: https://youtu.be/xxf-RtWO6-c

Nestled in Eastern Indonesia, Lamalera is a village defined by an ancient tradition: the hunting of whales. Passed down through generations, this practice is not merely a livelihood — it is the heartbeat of the community. But change is on the horizon. Young people are leaving to work and study in the cities, and pressure to abandon whaling grows ever louder.

At the centre of this story are four voices. Kris, a 15-year-old navigating high school and an uncertain future. Her father Karolous, a seasoned harpooner carrying the weight of tradition. Ignacious, a respected ship builder whose craft is inseparable from the hunt. And Sister Maria, a Catholic nun offering her own quiet perspective on a village in transition. Together, they open the doors of their world — offering an intimate, first-hand portrait of one of the last indigenous whaling cultures on earth, and revealing how every thread of life in Lamalera leads back to the sea.

snippet.title: Escaping Iraq: The Cost of Giving Up Everything for Safety | Bridging Boarders
snippet.description:
Over the past 20 years, grassroots sponsorship group NEST has helped bring dozens of displaced families to safety in Canada. In this moving episode of Bridging Borders, we follow the harrowing journey of Samur—an Iraqi academic with a Ph.D. in cyber security—and his young family. Targeted by violent militias who systematically hunt down intellectuals and professionals in post-war Iraq, the family spent four agonizing years stuck in limbo in Jordan, forbidden from working and unable to return home. Watch the emotional moment they finally touch down in Saskatoon to face a crowd of strangers holding balloons, a brand new home waiting for them next door, and the daunting challenge of starting over from absolute zero.

snippet.title: Germany's Underworld: From the Alps to the River Rhine
snippet.description:
Unlock the secrets of Germany’s rivers and lakes—discover bizarre animals, hidden caves, and epic freshwater predators in this stunning underwater journey!

Dive deep beneath the surface as we explore Germany’s mysterious aquatic world, from the snowy peaks of the Alps to the tidal reaches of the North Sea. Discover rare footage of diverse fish like the mighty northern pike and elusive Welsh catfish, delicate courtships, journeys of glacial meltwater, and ancient underwater relics. Venture through clear lakes such as Königsee and Lake Constance, uncovering extraordinary wildlife, from invasive jellyfish to prehistoric settlements, and learn how human activity has shaped this fragile ecosystem.

Follow the winding path of the Rhine as it carves dramatic gorges, waterfalls, and hidden canyons, home to curious salamanders, ancient fossils, and dazzling dragonflies. Reveal the wonders of submerged caves in the Swabian Alps, inhabited only by the bravest divers and rarest species. Witness fascinating natural cycles: mass frog and toad gatherings, unique breeding rituals, and the seasonal return of cranes as winter’s chill sets in. 

This documentary showcases the delicate balance of life underwater, evolutionary marvels, and the enduring impact of both nature and humans on these vibrant but threatened habitats. Perfect for fans of wildlife, ecology, and natural wonders, this is Germany as you’ve never seen it before—through the eyes of its remarkable waters.

snippet.title: War Factories: S03 EP04
snippet.description:
Think Porsche only means speed? Discover the secret history of Porsche in WWII tank design and the epic war of industrial production that shaped modern warfare.

Step inside the untold story of war production, where victory on the battlefield depended not just on military strategy, but on factory power. This video exposes how brands like Porsche, Skoda, and Rolls-Royce were forged in the fire of world wars—not just in racing circuits. Dive into the surprising journey of Ferdinand Porsche, who began as a pioneering electrical engineer and race car designer but became obsessed with crafting military muscle for the Nazi war machine. From the iconic Volkswagen Beetle to the notorious Panzer VIII Maus, see how Porsche’s ambition and partnership with Hitler led to engineering marvels—and catastrophic failures—for Germany’s war efforts.

Explore the innovation and missteps behind vehicles like the Kubelwagen, Ferdinand, Elephant, and JagdTiger, and learn how Porsche’s relentless pursuit of bigger, more powerful tanks ironically helped the Allies by draining Nazi resources. This video details the critical production battles of WWII—from the German struggle with mass manufacturing to the Soviet T-34’s game-changing design—and reveals why tank quality sometimes couldn’t match the importance of sheer quantity. Finally, trace how Porsche’s wartime legacy evolved into the legendary sports cars we know today, thanks to Ferry Porsche and the iconic 356 and 911 models. If you think you know Porsche, think again—this is the story of genius, ambition, and the high price of overengineering in the crucible of war.

snippet.title: War Factories: S03 EP05
snippet.description:
Modern wars aren’t won on the battlefield—they’re won in the factories. Discover how mass production, the Opel Blitz, and American industry shaped WWII’s outcome.

Dive deep into the hidden history of war production, where trucks—not tanks—became the unsung heroes of World War II. This video unpacks the incredible story of the Opel Blitz truck, its vital role in enabling Blitzkrieg, and the unexpected American connection: General Motors owned and operated Opel, Germany’s largest truck manufacturer, before and during Hitler’s rise. You’ll learn how GM, Ford, and other industrial titans navigated a complex web of politics, profit, and power struggles, sometimes supplying both sides of the war.

We trace the rise of German war manufacturing—from GM’s risky investment in Opel through the company’s transformation under Nazi rule. Uncover the brilliance of mass production at Brandenburg’s truck plant, the crucial role of synthetic fuels (with GM’s involvement), and the moral dilemmas and evasions faced by Allied corporations caught in wartime Germany. See how the humble truck became the backbone of modern warfare, why supply chains could decide victory or defeat, and how, ultimately, America’s unrivaled industrial capacity helped tip the scales against Hitler. Learn how GM and Ford factories turned out armies of trucks, tanks, and planes for both the Axis and Allies, and how postwar justice unfolded for foreign companies like GM.

Whether you’re fascinated by military history, the economics of war, or stories of corporate intrigue, this video offers a sweeping, nuanced look at the real engines of the Second World War.

Venezuela’s Lost Children | Surviving a Country in Collapse | Free Documentary

Ecuador - The Narco Wars: https://youtu.be/p3EdLKSLJYY

Corruption and mismanagement has turned Venezuela into a failed state. Over six million people have fled the country in recent years. Around one million children were left behind by their parents. This remarkable film follows two single mothers and their children over several months as they do what it takes to survive.

In the barrio Santa Rosa de Agua, health care has collapsed and children are dying from hunger. Carolina has set up a foundation to help feed them. But the barrio is so violent that she had to send her own daughter, Victoria, to a children’s home. The home is an oasis in the midst of violence and deprivation. However, many of the children, who haven’t seen their parents for years, are traumatised. They struggle with feelings of rejection.

Most people in the barrio survive through violence, prostitution and begging. “I’ve had to do lots of things for my kids,” confides Kiara, “selling drugs, stealing, prostituting myself – everything a woman can do for her children.” Her eldest son, Yorbenis, 14, has already joined a gang and is on the verge of his first kill. 

Desperate, Kiara decides to leave the country for Colombia. She takes her small children with her, while Yorbenis stays behind. Now, she’s terrified that he will be murdered in her absence. She knows he is being hunted by rival gangs as well as the police…

snippet.title: War Factories: S03 EP03
snippet.description:
Think World War II was won on the battlefield? Think again. Discover how the Skoda factory—and the power of mass production—shaped the fate of nations and the modern world.

Explore the untold story of war production, where the outcome of the 20th century’s greatest conflicts was decided not just by soldiers and generals, but by factories and the relentless race to outproduce the enemy. This video dives deep into the pivotal role of the Skoda Works, tracing its rise from an ambitious steel plant in Bohemia to one of Europe’s largest armaments factories, supplying heavy artillery, tanks, and engineering expertise across multiple empires. Uncover how brands like Porsche, Rolls Royce, and Skoda honed their reputation through wartime innovation—and how the Nazi regime coveted Skoda’s production power above all.

But at the heart of this factory’s story is an incredible tale of resistance and redemption. Led by Albert Göring, brother to infamous Nazi Hermann Göring, the Skoda factory became ground zero for sabotage from within. While outwardly collaborating with the Nazis, Albert secretly rescued dozens of Jews and members of the resistance, orchestrated passive sabotage, and undermined German tank production—all while narrowly escaping repeated arrests and a Gestapo death warrant. Witness testimony at Nuremberg would reveal the extent of his covert actions, challenging the simple narratives of hero and villain.

From supplying the Austro-Hungarian Empire and fueling the Blitzkrieg with the LT-35 tank to surviving Allied bombing and transforming into a car manufacturer under communism and capitalism alike, Skoda stands as a testament to the enduring influence of industry on history. If you want to know how wars are truly won—and how one factory defied the odds—this is a must-watch.

If you’re looking for a comprehensive, visually stunning account of the origins and evolution of the Korean War—often overlooked despite its profound impact—this immersive experience is essential viewing.
